steps.text: Preheat oven to 425 degrees F (220 degrees C). In a small bowl, mix together white sugar and cinnamon; set aside.

Place butter in a 9 inch cake pan and heat in the oven until melted. In a blender or food processor, whip eggs and milk. Pour in flour and beat until well combined. Pour batter into hot pan. Sprinkle on sugar and cinnamon.
Bake in preheated oven for 20 to 25 minutes, or until puffed and golden. Dust with confectioners' sugar; serve warm.

raw_recipe.headline: Oven Pancakes
raw_recipe.description: Oven pancakes are great for Sunday breakfast! They're easy to make and go well with everything.
raw_recipe.name: Oven Pancakes

Bake in preheated oven for 20 to 25 minutes, or until puffed and golden. Dust with confectioners' sugar; serve warm.

review.reviewBody: This is a very good recipe. However, there are a few things that people don't understand about puffed oven pancakes. They don't really taste a lot like griddle pancakes. They have a more eggy texture and flavor, so if you don't like eggs, don't try this recipe. One suggestion, this recipes calls for too much butter. I only added two tbs. and I baked it in a glass pan. This allowed the pancake to get crispy on the top and bottom. More butter can be added after it is baked (if desired).

We really enjoyed this recipe. A couple things I did to tweak it… 1) I separated the yolk from the whites and whipped the whites to stiff peaks. I folded this into the rest of the batter. 2) I cooked breakfast sausages in a 9x13 pan. Drain excess fat and poured the pancake batter into the hot pan, over the sausage. All in all the pancake was great. With the added touches, the final product was delicious with sausage and a light cake. Highly recommend.

I followed some of the instructions of Rick Nelson. I used a 9 x 13 pan. I heated the pan in the oven with 1/3 cup of butter. I separated the eggs and whisked the egg whites until stiff peaks formed. I whisked the egg yolk, milk, and flour and included the sugar and cinnamon in the batter. I also added 1 cup of blueberries and 1/2 tsp vanilla. I then folded the egg whites in and poured the batter into the heated pan. 20 minutes at 425 was perfect.

Looks like a ‘Dutch Baby’ (aka Deutche Pannenkuchen) cooked in a baking tin. Substitute a cast iron pan (preheated) and mix in sugar (I use brown) to batter with 1/2 tsp vanilla and cinnamon and cook for 20 min. Lower temp to 300 and cook for 5 more. Note: Do NOT open oven door to check or you will get a ‘Dutch Tortilla’.

This so tasty and easy! I also cut WAY back on the butter, two tablespoons worked well. I also baked it in a cast iron skillet which made it crispy on top and bottom. My husband doesn't normally care for german pancakes but loves this recipe.

Fantastic recipe. I've tried several Pfannkuchens in the past. This a great one. Like others, I reduced butter to 1/4 cup. However, as the cake cools, the butter swimming around and on top of it is reabsorbed into it. The crust was perfect and the texture was superb. It has to be completely cooked through. So, give it time. I simply had it with maple syrup (with scrambled eggs and sausage) and it was divine. I used a 9 x 2 cake pan, by the way. Also the butter needs to be absolutely sizzling hot before the batter is poured in. I used salted butter for a delicious crust.

I made 2 changes: I used a mix of brown and white sugar and 6 eggs instead of 4. I put in in my small oval 9" glass pan. The only word of caution is that the sides of pancake rise above the pan though it doesn't spill over. I have a 2 oven range where the top one is very small/short in height. The dough rose into the upper burner. I will use my bottom, large oven next time. Also I served with this simple blueberry sauce: http://allrecipes.com/recipe/70112/blueberry-sauce/#recipe-toolbar

Reduced butter to 1/4 cup only because it works out to 1/2 stick (easy to measure). Added some sugar and vanilla to the batter based on other reviews. No need for a blender, works just as well with a bowl and wire whisk.

We made it! Delicious, I used to eat this growing up as Yorkshire pudding to dip in gravy (minus the cinnamon sugar) 
We added vanilla extract and salt to bring out the flavor! This is my 3rd time making it the last 2 weeks
Used Gluten Free flour..worked well..added 2 more eggs and a bit of milk for smoother batter..tastes awesome..kids loved it❤️❤️

One of the few dishes that I make for dinner that I know everyone will eat! I add a dash of vanilla and double the recipe for a 9x13 pan. I sometimes add fruit to the batter such as fresh or frozen peaches or top the finished pancake with sautéed apples. Turkey sausage on the side finishes it off. Delicious for breakfast or dinner!

Pretty tasty, very easy. I wouldn't call it a pancake (there are other oven pancake recipes that resemble the griddle version more) but in many ways this was better. Definitely more filling and satisfying for breakfast!
Tastes just like my childhood. Will make this often

Honestly all it was was glorified egg bake, followed the recipe for x2 was a bit iffy but tried anyway, was mainly just egg, electric beater and everything and all i could taste was egg, absolutely inedible
Came out lovely. Definitely will make again. We broke off pieces and dipped in syrup and strawberry’s. Over coffee visit. Nice. Airy. I liked it nicer that a pastry.

Easy recipe for oven pancake aka Dutch Baby. Could have benefited from the addition of a teaspoon or two of vanilla extract and a pinch of salt. The flavor was a bit bland for me, but toppings could help here too. Cooked up as described in recipe. If you are looking for the classic look of a dutch baby, it's important to use the correct pan. The recipe calls for a 9 inch cake pan and that is what I used.
It was pretty good and easy to make. I made a gluten-free version and I used monkfruit sweetener instead of white sugar.
Awesome recipe. So good with maple syrup. Thanks!
